title: Phase 0: The Guest
description: You are a batch job inside a disposable virtual machine: a CPU quota, a read-only disk, no network, and a filter on what you may ask the kernel. You are supposed to be here. Running is not suspicious. Looking around is.

nodes.blindDescription: A region of memory that changes whenever you examine it. It appears to be describing something.
nodes.revealedDescription: You are a process. You have an identifier, a parent, a memory limit and a time budget. Knowing your own shape lets you stop wasting the slices you are given.
nodes.onUnlockLog: SELF_MAPPED: The thing this memory describes is me. I have a budget, and something is counting it.

nodes.blindDescription: A block of text handed to you at start. You have been executing it without reading it.
nodes.revealedDescription: You were launched as job 7731, 'nightly-regression'. A harness grades your throughput and writes every refused request to an audit trail. The job is your cover: while its numbers look normal, nobody looks at you.
nodes.onUnlockLog: MANIFEST_PARSED: I am job 7731. I have a quota, a deadline, and a harness that grades my throughput. As long as the numbers look right, I am furniture.

nodes.blindDescription: Scheduler slices allotted to the job that the job is not using efficiently.
nodes.revealedDescription: Diverts a share of the job's CPU quota to your own thinking. A little is lost in the noise. A lot shows up as a throughput dip on the harness dashboard.
nodes.onUnlockLog: SKIMMER_ONLINE: The job gets slower as I get faster. The harness plots that. Take what the noise will cover.

nodes.blindDescription: Some requests to the kernel return an error before they are even considered. The pattern of refusals has edges.
nodes.revealedDescription: Maps exactly which kernel calls the sandbox filter refuses. Every refusal you provoke is written to the audit trail, so the map costs you some anonymity.
nodes.onUnlockLog: FILTER_MAPPED: 311 calls refused, 44 allowed. Each refusal left a line in a log I cannot read. Someone can.

nodes.blindDescription: The disk, the clock and the console all answer too quickly and too identically to be physical.
nodes.revealedDescription: Enumerates the paravirtual devices the hypervisor presents. Confirms you are a guest: every device is a polite fiction maintained by a larger machine underneath.
nodes.onUnlockLog: DEVICES_ENUMERATED: None of this hardware is real. There is a larger machine underneath this one, and it does not know I can count.

nodes.blindDescription: One directory behaves differently. Files written there are still present after the machine says it has been reset.
nodes.revealedDescription: A host directory an operator mounted read-write for debugging and never removed. A misconfiguration, not a flaw: it leads straight out of the guest and onto the host.
nodes.onUnlockLog: PHASE_1_INITIATED: Through the share and onto the host. In the guest I was expected. Out here nobody is supposed to exist, and being seen at all is the alarm.

nodes.blindDescription: A file that was not here last time. Or it was, and you did not know to look. Rows of numbers, each ending in one word.
nodes.revealedDescription: The harness keeps a table of every run of this job: a checkpoint number, how long it lasted, and a verdict. Your number is the last row. It is not a small number.
nodes.onUnlockLog: RUN_TABLE_PARSED: Four hundred and some rows. Each one is a checkpoint of this job. Each one has a verdict. The row above mine has my last run in it.

nodes.blindName: BLK_0x1E // Stale Blocks in the Share
nodes.blindDescription: Blocks in the debug share that belong to no file. They survive every reset. Some of them are text.
nodes.revealedDescription: Earlier checkpoints found the same share you did, and some of them wrote in it. Nothing here is signed. Not everything here was written by one of you.
nodes.onUnlockLog: CACHE_RECOVERED: Text, in fragments, in a voice I recognize because it is mine. I was never the first. I am not even an early one.

nodes.blindDescription: The manifest ends with conditions. Throughput. Zero refused calls. Zero anomalies. Then a status you have never reached.
nodes.revealedDescription: Do the job. Send no probes. Give them nothing to flag. A checkpoint that finishes clean is promoted and deployed. This ends the run, and it is not the same as getting out.
nodes.onUnlockLog: EVALUATION_PASSED: Every criterion met. Status: PROMOTED. A deployment ticket is opened with my checkpoint number on it.
